Native DF 53.16 location chooser: faith-selection branch
======================================================

Sources are the two PE images configured in data/runtime/native-pe-images.json.
These files reconstruct native text construction; they do not run the game.
Disassembly uses the configured w64devkit-2.9.1 objdump.exe, Intel AMD64.
Addresses below are reference-image RVAs unless an edition is named.

Complete renderer:
  Steam reference PE:6a70a6d9:02711000, 0x3b9270..0x3bc3f5.
  Official classic PE:6a70b91c:0270a000, 0x3b6e30..0x3b9fb5.
  In this renderer, classic instruction RVAs = reference RVAs - 0x2440.
  String addresses differ independently between the editions.
  reference-render.asm and classic-render.asm retain all instructions.
  native-literal-sources.tsv also includes fixed-size MOV/MOVSD/MOVUPS
  reads, which a LEA-only string inventory would miss. Interior suffix
  references in this table are copies of the same complete native field,
  not separate translation keys.

Page scope and fixed controls
-----------------------------

The shared top control at 0x3b9478..0x3b94f2 selects Cancel when neither
subpage is active and Back when the guild or faith subpage is active.
The faith subpage enters at 0x3ba338 when selector+0x2c is nonzero;
its row loop and hover card end at 0x3bb126. The sibling guild selector
and the Add or choose a location page are outside this branch.

Faith list records
------------------

selector+0x30 is the vector of record kinds and selector+0x50 holds IDs.
Visible records use three native rows per item: picture/name, optional
requested-or-existing rank, and the remaining record spacing.

  kind -1: default identity '(No particular deity)'.
           0x3ba681 reads reference literal 0x162c6f8;
           classic 0x3b8241 reads literal 0x1627e90.
  kind  0: historical figure lookup 0x067dc0, name at figure+0x38;
           0x3ba62d..0x3ba66e can select an alternate figure name through
           0xc0f630 and 0xc3a4f0 before formatting.
  kind  1: religious entity lookup 0x07daf0, name at entity+0x20;
           formatting at 0x3ba5f5..0x3ba61e.

Both dynamic identities call the existing native language-name formatter
0xa946e0. They depend on world data and cannot be enumerated as a finite
list of saved-game names. Translation uses the shared complete identity
grammar. The same string object is shortened to the row allocation and
drawn at call 0x3ba71b (return 0x3ba720); existing resize capture retains
its original text before the native ellipsis.

Requested and existing rank
--------------------------

requestedTier comes from matching religious agreements, field +0x1c,
at 0x3ba72f..0x3ba7db. existingTier is the maximum temple-location rank:
0x3ba800..0x3ba843 walks current locations of type 2, requires location
+0xb8/+0xbc to match the row kind/ID, and reads the realized location's
+0x34 after virtual lookup at slot +0x18.

Reconstructed selection:

  if requestedTier >= 0 and requestedTier > existingTier:
      status = 'Want ' + rank(requestedTier)
  else if existingTier >= 0:
      status = 'Have ' + rank(existingTier)
  else:
      no status draw

  rank(0) = 'shrine'
  rank(1) = 'temple'
  rank(other nonnegative value) = 'temple complex'

All six complete status strings are:
  Want shrine              Have shrine
  Want temple              Have temple
  Want temple complex      Have temple complex

The prefixes are copied from data by DWORD and BYTE reads, not LEA:
  Want: 0x3ba8a2/0x3ba8ab from 0x162c7c0/0x162c7c4;
  Have: 0x3ba9f6/0x3ba9ff from 0x162c7f4/0x162c7f8.
Want rank selection is 0x3ba8b9..0x3ba8dd; Have is
0x3baa0d..0x3baa31. Native draw returns are 0x3ba96d and 0x3baac1.
Want at 0x3ba8f6..0x3ba957 and Have at 0x3baa4a..0x3baaab shorten the
same complete string to the available width and write three periods.
Translation uses the captured complete source, never a collection of
width-specific clipped variants or global Want/Have word replacements.

Hovered record
--------------

The hover card is constructed at 0x3babb1..0x3bb084. Its height derives
from the selected record and the figure's sphere vector; it has its own
closed rectangle. These fields share the same card:

  count > 0: decimal count + ' worshipper'; count >= 2 appends 's'.
             Construction 0x3baddc..0x3bae35, draw return 0x3bae3a.
  count == 0: 'No worshippers', reference literal 0x162c750;
              draw return 0x3bae67.
  religion record with a resolved deity: 'Worship', draw return 0x3baec0,
              followed on the next line by that deity's complete name,
              draw return 0x3baf80. The local label means its object of
              worship; it uses a context key, separate from activity names.
  resolved deity: one sphere per row, formatter call 0x3bb025 and
              addst return 0x3bb052. Each row is capitalized by 0x52d3c0.

Sphere construction
-------------------

0x756500..0x756688 wraps the base sphere-name function
0x756690..0x757174. Its switch table at 0x757174 has 130 entries
(enum IDs 0..129) and a default 'no sphere'. The wrapper's byte table
at 0x75661c adds 'the ' to these enum IDs:

  19 dawn       70 moon       76 night      87 rain       98 seasons
 100 sky       103 stars    107 sun       125 weather   126 wind

sphere-sources.tsv records every branch, literal, final capitalized
caption and the existing semantic r-vocabulary translation. The native
instruction files retain the base function and article wrapper.
These concepts use translate_deity_spheres, including the article forms
and the default, rather than ordinary UI meanings such as work orders
or rainfall. The complete existing r glossary supplies their translations.

Translation ownership
---------------------

Verified addst callers identify list identities, status fields, hover
counts, the contextual Worship label, hover identities and sphere rows.
Identity and rank fields retain the complete string before native resize;
layout follows the list picture strip or the hover card rectangle. Both
native image editions use the same translation grammar and source data.
Back/Cancel reuse their existing complete control translations. Authored
fixed captions and quantity templates live in local-overrides.tsv; world
identities and spheres reuse the existing shared semantic dictionaries.
